lastCompletedGameRecap.recapHeadline: Jared Goff throws 2 TDs, Jahmyr Gibbs runs for 2 more and Lions beat Bucs 31-21 for 6th straight win
lastCompletedGameRecap.recapLeadExcerpt: DETROIT -- — The Detroit Lions are finding their groove, leaning on a balanced attack offensively and a steadily improving defense that hasn't been hurt by the losses of Aidan Hutchinson and Jack Campbell .  Jared Goff threw two touchdown passes through three quarters and Jahmyr Gibbs ran for two scores in the fourth, helping Detroit pull away and beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 31-21 on Sunday.  “We’re continuing to climb and it’s the right time,” coach Dan Campbell said.  The Lions (8-2) have won six straight, setting up a pivotal NFC North game against the Chicago Bears (8-2) in a matchup of first-place teams on Thanksgiving to kick off the NFL's tripleheader on the holiday. ” NFL history Lions edge rusher Ahmed Hassanein became the first Egyptian to play in an NFL game, making his debut in the league after Detroit drafted the former Boise State star in the sixth round in 2025.

injuryReport.name: Roschon Johnson
factors: Officially ruled Out on weekly game status report
injuryReport.beatComment: Johnson injured his ankle in Sunday's win over the Saints and with the quick turnaround for Week 12, he won't be available against the Lions. The Bears will roll with D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai as their only healthy backs for Thursday's game.

injuryReport.name: Elijah Hicks
factors: Officially ruled Out on weekly game status report
injuryReport.beatComment: Hicks was not listed on Monday's injury report, but he was unable to practice Tuesday due to a concussion. He's mostly played on special teams this season, but his absence thins the Bears' depth at safety behind starters Cam Lewis and rookie first-rounder Dillon Thieneman. Hicks' next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Jaguars on Sunday, Dec. 6.

factors: Late-week injury addition (added Friday Limited after clean Wed–Thu; base prior 76%)

He has accumulated 34 tackles (23 solo) and four pass defenses through eight regular-season games.

coachingMatchup.headline: Dan Campbell & DC Kelvin Sheppard vs. HC Ben Johnson, OC Press Taylor & DC Dennis Allen (Ford Field)
coachingMatchup.summary: Week 12 two-sided coordinator chess match pitting Detroit Lions's staff (Dan Campbell, OC Drew Petzing, DC Kelvin Sheppard) against Chicago Bears (8-2)—testing both Detroit's offensive efficiency and its defensive pass-rush and coverage discipline.
bullets: Pass-Game Efficiency & Coverage Shell Delta: Dan Campbell and OC Drew Petzing pair condensed splits with pre-snap jet motion and orbit motion to stress Chicago Bears's single-high vs. two-high rotations—widening curl/flat defenders to attack the honey-hole between hook/curl linebackers and deep safeties on play-action choice/dagger concepts.

Trench Run-Fit & Two-Way Leverage: Against Chicago Bears's pin-and-pull, counter, and duo runs targeting the A- and B-gaps, DC Kelvin Sheppard balances four-man pressure with disguised Quarters and Cover 6 split-safety rotations on early downs and in the red zone.

Money-Down & Red-Zone Execution: Third-down conversion discipline and red-zone touchdown rate govern whether Detroit sustains multi-play scoring drives or yields momentum to Chicago Bears's pass rush and coverage disguises.
Tempo, Turnovers & Venue Leverage: Ford Field situational play-calling, penalty margin, and turnover differential provide the clearest late-game swing factors for both coaching staffs.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Jared Goff, Sam LaPorta & Jameson Williams vs. CB Jaylon Johnson & LB Devin Bush
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: DET: #5 Pass Off (259.6 yds) · #5 Off. Scoring (+8.10) | CHI: #9 Pass Def (-1.08)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Jared Goff, Sam LaPorta & Jameson Williams attack the intermediate seams and middle-of-the-field leverage windows against Chicago Bears's #9 pass defense (-1.08). Winning early-down timing throws keeps Detroit's offense ahead of the chains and punishes disguised single-high rotations.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch Jared Goff (#16) scanning Bears's deep safeties at the snap—when LB Devin Bush widens to take away the crossers, the intermediate seam opens immediately for Sam LaPorta (#87).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Alim McNeill, Tyleik Williams & Derrick Moore vs. QB Caleb Williams & OT Theo Benedet
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: DET: #16 Def Sacks (2.3/gm) | CHI: #16 Pass Protection (6.5%)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Alim McNeill, Tyleik Williams & Derrick Moore lead Detroit's #16 NFL pass rush (2.3/gm) against Chicago Bears's #16 pass-protection unit (6.5%). Collapsing the interior pocket without sending extra blitzers lets Lions keep seven defenders in coverage.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: On 3rd-and-6+, watch whether Alim McNeill (#54) draw chip help from Bears's tight ends or backs—creating 1-on-1 rush lanes inside for Tyleik Williams (#91).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: D.J. Reed, Chuck Clark & Derrick Barnes vs. WR Luther Burden III & QB Caleb Williams
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: DET: #23 Pass Def (+3.65) | CHI: #14 Pass Off (233.4 yds)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: D.J. Reed, Chuck Clark & Derrick Barnes anchor Detroit's #23 pass defense (+3.65) against WR Luther Burden III and Chicago Bears's #14 passing attack (233.4 yds). Limiting explosive 20+ yard chunk plays forces Bears into sustained red-zone drives.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Track D.J. Reed (#4) at the top of routes against WR Luther Burden III: press-bail alignment with safety help over the top takes away QB Caleb Williams's preferred isolation shots.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Jahmyr Gibbs & Amon-Ra St. Brown vs. Bears Front Seven & LB Devin Bush
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: DET: #8 Rush Off (132.2 yds) | CHI: #18 Rush Def (-0.55)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Jahmyr Gibbs & Amon-Ra St. Brown test Chicago Bears's #18 run defense (-0.55) with horizontal stretch and interior cutback lanes. Generating 4.5+ yards on first down unlocks play-action explosives and neutralizes Bears's pass-rush packages.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch whether Bears's linebackers over-pursue motion to the perimeter—opening decisive backside B-gap cutback lanes for Jahmyr Gibbs (#0).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Blake Miller, Tate Ratledge & Penei Sewell vs. DE Montez Sweat & Bears Simulated Pressures
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: DET: #16 Pass Protection (6.0%) | CHI: #16 Def Sacks (2.4/gm)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Blake Miller, Tate Ratledge & Penei Sewell protect Jared Goff (#16 protection at 6.0%) against DE Montez Sweat and Chicago Bears's #16 pass rush (2.4/gm). Passing off interior twists and simulated blitzes cleanly determines late-down conversion efficiency.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch Blake Miller (#76) on obvious passing downs—if DE Montez Sweat cannot win clean around the arc, Bears must dial up interior stunts that stress Tate Ratledge (#69).
